verdict.rationale: Gusto's official CLI documents first-class headless and scripted use. CI can authenticate via GUSTO_ACCESS_TOKEN and GUSTO_COMPANY_UUID env vars or --token-stdin, and gets a stable JSON envelope automatically when stdout is piped, documented exit codes, --dry-run previews and a separate sandbox environment. This is backed by verified install endpoints and releases. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of an actual CI pipeline run, and the CLI only drafts payroll (no submit command; agent-mode writes need --confirm).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Headless/scripted operation is first-class: besides interactive OAuth (gusto auth login / gusto auth whoami), CI and scripted environments can pass GUSTO_ACCESS_TOKEN + GUSTO_COMPANY_UUID env vars or pipe the token on stdin (--token-stdin, keeping the secret out of argv, shell history, and set -x/audit logs).
--agent/--json (auto-on when stdout is piped) emits a stable JSON envelope {ok, data|error}; documented exit codes 0-9; --dry-run previews any create request
installs to ~/.gusto/bin/gusto with no sudo, and updates PATH; GUSTO_CLI_VERSION pins a release, GUSTO_INSTALL_DIR relocates.
